chapter.chapter_title: The present participle and the gerund

attestations.source_text: The present participle. You have used the participe passé (past participle) many times with the compound tenses. Another participle is the participe présent (present participle).
VOCABULAIRE
The gerund. When the present participle is introduced by en, it is referred to as the gérondif (gerund).

concepts.name: present participle
concepts.description: Participe présent: verb form ending in -ant, used as verb, noun, or adjective.

attestations.source_text: Another participle is the participe présent (present participle).

concepts.name: present participle as noun, adjective, verb
concepts.description: The present participle can function as a noun (with gender/number agreement), as an adjective (agreeing with noun), or as a verb (invariable).

attestations.source_text: Some participes présents can be used as nouns... Many participes présents can be used as adjectives... The participe présent can also be used as a verb.

concepts.name: spelling changes in present participle
concepts.description: Some -cer and -ger verbs have spelling changes when forming the present participle.

attestations.source_text: Some spelling changes occur with some -cer and -ger verbs.

concepts.name: irregular present participles
concepts.description: Three verbs have irregular present participles: être, avoir, savoir.

attestations.source_text: Three verbs have an irregular present participle: être -> étant, avoir -> ayant, savoir -> sachant.

concepts.name: pronominal present participle
concepts.description: Pronominal verbs form the present participle with a reflexive pronoun corresponding to the subject.

attestations.source_text: Pronominal verbs follow the same pattern. Do not forget the pronoun corresponding to the subject.

concepts.name: perfect participle
concepts.description: Construction with ayant or étant + past participle to express anteriority.

attestations.source_text: When an action precedes another one, avoir and être in the participe présent can be combined with a participe passé.

concepts.name: gerund
concepts.description: Gérondif: en + present participle, expresses relationship between two actions.

attestations.source_text: When the present participle is introduced by en, it is referred to as the gérondif (gerund).

concepts.name: gerund meanings
concepts.description: The gerund can express simultaneity, manner, condition, or causality.

attestations.source_text: It can express simultaneity, manner, condition, or causality.

grammar_rules.summary: The present participle is formed by dropping the -ons ending from the present tense nous form and adding -ant.
grammar_rules.explanation: For example: nous chantons -> chantant, nous partons -> partant, nous choisissons -> choisissant, nous buvons -> buvant, nous voyons -> voyant, nous répondons -> répondant.
exceptions: irregular present participles: être, avoir, savoir
common_traps: do not forget spelling changes for -cer/-ger

attestations.source_text: It is formed by dropping the -ons ending from the present tense nous form and adding -ant.

grammar_rules.summary: Some -cer and -ger verbs change spelling in the present participle: -cer becomes -çant, -ger becomes -geant.
grammar_rules.explanation: Examples: commencer -> commençant, influencer -> influençant, manger -> mangeant, nager -> nageant.
grammar_rules.formation: For -cer: replace c with ç before -ant; for -ger: insert e before -ant
common_traps: forgetting to change c to ç or g to ge

attestations.source_text: Some spelling changes occur with some -cer and -ger verbs: commencer -> commençant, influencer -> influençant, manger -> mangeant, nager -> nageant.

grammar_rules.summary: Pronominal verbs follow the same pattern, but include the reflexive pronoun corresponding to the subject.
grammar_rules.explanation: Example with se promener: me promenant, te promenant, se promenant, nous promenant, vous promenant, se promenant.

attestations.source_text: Pronominal verbs follow the same pattern. Do not forget the pronoun corresponding to the subject. Let's look at the present participle of se promener.

grammar_rules.summary: Three verbs have irregular present participles: être -> étant, avoir -> ayant, savoir -> sachant.
common_traps: do not apply regular rule to these verbs

attestations.source_text: Three verbs have an irregular present participle: être -> étant, avoir -> ayant, savoir -> sachant.

grammar_rules.rule_name: Present participle used as a noun
grammar_rules.summary: Some present participles can be used as nouns; when used as a noun, they change according to gender and number.
grammar_rules.explanation: Examples: un gagnant/une gagnante, un perdant/une perdante.
grammar_rules.formation: present participle as noun with gender/number agreement
common_traps: do not leave invariable when used as noun

attestations.source_text: Some participes présents can be used as nouns. When used as a noun, the present participle changes according to gender and number.

grammar_rules.rule_name: Present participle used as an adjective
grammar_rules.summary: Many present participles can be used as adjectives; they agree with the noun they modify.
grammar_rules.explanation: Examples: des matchs épuisants, un commentateur fascinant, un sport exigeant, une pièce amusante.
agreement_rules: agrees in gender and number with noun

attestations.source_text: Many participes présents can be used as adjectives. When used as an adjective, the participe présent agrees with the noun it modifies.

grammar_rules.rule_name: Present participle used as a verb
grammar_rules.summary: When used as a verb, the present participle is invariable.
grammar_rules.explanation: Examples: La police l'a aperçu entrant dans un laboratoire médical. Étant blessé au genou, il n'a pas pu jouer.

attestations.source_text: The participe présent can also be used as a verb. Note that when used as a verb, the present participle is invariable.

grammar_rules.summary: When an action precedes another, use avoir or être in the present participle combined with a past participle. The past participle agrees with the subject if the verb is conjugated with être.
grammar_rules.explanation: Forms: ayant vu, ayant compris, ayant joué, ayant traversé, étant allé(e)(s), étant parti(e)(s), nous étant promené(e)s, nous étant retrouvé(e)s.
agreement_rules: past participle agrees with subject if auxiliary is être

attestations.source_text: When an action precedes another one, avoir and être in the participe présent can be combined with a participe passé. Note that the past participle agrees with the subject of the sentence if the verb is conjugated with être.

grammar_rules.summary: The gerund is formed with en + the present participle.
usage: to describe relationship between two actions

attestations.source_text: It is formed with en + the present participle.

grammar_rules.rule_name: Gerund expressing simultaneity, manner, condition, causality
grammar_rules.summary: The gerund can express simultaneity, manner, condition, or causality.
grammar_rules.explanation: Examples: Il s'est foulé la cheville en jouant au foot (simultaneity). Elle écoute de la musique en conduisant (simultaneity). M. Vincent a gagné beaucoup d'argent en achetant ces toiles (manner/causality). En renvoyant ce joueur, vous feriez une grosse erreur (condition).

attestations.source_text: It can express simultaneity, manner, condition, or causality.

grammar_rules.summary: When tout precedes the gerund, it underscores a tension or contradiction between two actions.
grammar_rules.explanation: Examples: Tout en étant un bon joueur, il ne marquait jamais de but. Tout en faisant semblant d'écouter le professeur, il jouait avec son iPod. Tout en pleurant, il riait. Tout en prétendant le contraire, elle voulait être élue.
common_traps: do not interpret as simple simultaneity

attestations.source_text: When tout precedes the gerund, it underscores a tension, a contradiction between two actions.

exceptions_and_traps.title: Spelling changes with -cer and -ger verbs in present participle
exceptions_and_traps.description: Some -cer and -ger verbs change spelling when forming the present participle: -cer becomes -çant (e.g., commencer -> commençant), and -ger becomes -geant (e.g., manger -> mangeant).

attestations.source_text: Some spelling changes occur with some -cer and -ger verbs: commencer -> commençant, influencer -> influençant, manger -> mangeant, nager -> nageant.

exceptions_and_traps.title: Irregular present participles (être, avoir, savoir)
exceptions_and_traps.description: Three verbs have irregular present participles: être -> étant, avoir -> ayant, savoir -> sachant. They do not follow the regular -ant rule.

attestations.source_text: Three verbs have an irregular present participle: être -> étant, avoir -> ayant, savoir -> sachant.

exceptions_and_traps.title: Present participle agreement depends on function
exceptions_and_traps.description: The present participle agrees when used as a noun (gender/number) or adjective (with noun), but is invariable when used as a verb.
exceptions_and_traps.correct_form: noun: un gagnant/une gagnante; adjective: des matchs épuisants; verb: invariable (e.g., entrant)
exceptions_and_traps.incorrect_form: using adjective agreement for verb use or vice versa

attestations.source_text: Some participes présents can be used as nouns... Many participes présents can be used as adjectives... The participe présent can also be used as a verb. Note that when used as a verb, the present participle is invariable.

exceptions_and_traps.title: Past participle agreement in perfect participle with être
exceptions_and_traps.description: In the perfect participle construction (ayant/étant + past participle), the past participle agrees with the subject if the auxiliary is être. Example: étant allé(e)(s), étant parti(e)(s).
exceptions_and_traps.correct_form: étant allée (feminine singular), étant partis (masculine plural)
exceptions_and_traps.incorrect_form: étant allé (without agreement for feminine subject)

attestations.source_text: Note that the past participle agrees with the subject of the sentence if the verb is conjugated with être.

exceptions_and_traps.title: Tout + gerund expresses contradiction, not just simultaneity
exceptions_and_traps.description: When tout precedes the gerund, it underscores tension or contradiction between two actions, not simple simultaneity.
exceptions_and_traps.correct_form: Tout en étant un bon joueur, il ne marquait jamais de but.
exceptions_and_traps.incorrect_form: Interpreting as simple simultaneity: 'While being a good player' without contradiction.

attestations.source_text: When tout precedes the gerund, it underscores a tension, a contradiction between two actions.
